rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis argues that he is better than Adam, so it would be improper for him to bow to someone inferior; this is his stated reason for refusing.
rows.anchor: Yani daha faziletli, daha yükseğim. Böyle olanın mâdûnuna secde etmesi ise revâ değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis supports his superiority claim by contrasting his creation from fire with Adam's creation from clay, assuming the better material makes its creature better.
rows.anchor: Ateş ise çamurdan hayırlıdır, hayırlıdan halk olunan da hayırlıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration command was the first test that made divine command conflict with Iblis's own wishes and exposed his true nature.
rows.anchor: bu hepsi için bir imtihan olmuş ve bu imtihan İblis’in hissiyâtına dokunmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's earlier company with the angels did not mean he truly had their obedience; until this test, God's command and his own desire had not conflicted.
rows.anchor: vasfını hakikaten hâiz olduğu için değil, emr-i ilâhî ile emr-i nefsin te‘âruz etmediğinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis had in fact served his own pleasure rather than God, as his first response to a command against his wishes reveals.
rows.anchor: İblis hakikatte Allah’a değil, kendi zevkine ta‘abbüd edermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He joins a true premise about their materials to a false claim of superiority, concealing invalid major premises and presenting desire as a logical conclusion; this is the first example of satanic sophistry.
rows.anchor: sâdık olan kaziyye-i hilkatten kâzib olan أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ da‘vâ-yı nefsânîsini istintâca kalkışmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satanic deception disguises refusal of good as knowledge by blending ignorance with learning, falsehood with truth, evil with good, and pride with flattery.
rows.anchor: hayırdan imtinâ‘ı tasvib için cehl ile ilmi, kizb ile sıdkı, şer ile hayrı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First, Iblis misjudges his role in answering the question: he argues back and accuses instead of admitting fault and apologizing.
rows.anchor: İtiraf ve i‘tizâr yerine itiraz ve tahtı’eye kalkışmıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, Iblis resorts to analogy and independent reasoning where an explicit command governs, appealing to creation as a counterargument.
rows.anchor: Mevrid-i nasta kıyas ve ictihâda kıyam etmiş, emr-i sarîhe karşı halkın delâletine müracaat eylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Iblis's account of their materials is true, he judges only by substance and ignores God's special honor to Adam, the spirit and form bestowed on him, and his vicegerent purpose.
rows.anchor: yalnız madde ve unsura itibar etmek isteyen İblis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The learned person's habit of narrowing attention to matter follows a path characteristic of Iblis.
rows.anchor: maddeye kasr-ı nazar mesleki mesâlik-i İblistendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither hidden premise is universally true: both creatures are equally created and subject to the Creator, and earth's qualities are more comprehensive and perfect than fire's.
rows.anchor: ikinci kaziyye külliyetiyle sâdık olmadığı gibi birinci kaziyye de ıtlâkıyla doğru değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a moral comparison, fire suggests lightness, anger, turmoil, and pride, while earth suggests dignity, patience, steadiness, gentleness, modesty, and generosity.
rows.anchor: türâbın vakār ü sekîneti, sabr u mekânet ve sebâtı, hilm ü hayâ ve semâhati

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His flawed induction and self-sourced understanding keep Iblis from seeing Adam as God's chosen manifestation and himself as an accursed one.
rows.anchor: ilmi Hak’tan değil nefsinden ahz etmek davasında bulunduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to descend means leaving either the garden where Iblis stood or the company of the angels.
rows.anchor: o bulunduğun cennetten yahut zümre-i melâike içinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated station is reserved for those who know their limits and obey with humility, so Iblis cannot remain there in arrogance.
rows.anchor: O makām-ı ulvî haddini bilen ehl-i tâat ve tevâzu‘a mahsustur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride makes a person small: whoever exalts himself inevitably falls, becomes low, and is humiliated.
rows.anchor: Tekebbür küçüklüktür, büyüyecek olan büyüklenmez, büyüklenen behemehâl küçülür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God immediately strips Iblis of his station, showing in practice that every creature's qualities are gifts from God rather than inherent possessions.
rows.anchor: bütün havâss-ı eşyânın mücerred bir dâd-ı Hak olduğunu bu suretle bir lemhada fiilen anlatıverdi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing immediate destruction, Iblis chooses continued life even in humiliation and asks to be kept alive until the resurrection of Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: zillet ü hakāretle olsun hayâtı memâta tercih ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the requested resurrection day with the second trumpet blast, linking it to the resurrection scenes in al-Zumar and al-Mutaffifin.
rows.anchor: [el-Mutaffifîn 83/6][^18] olan nefha-i sâniye vaktidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's request shows that he believed in the Creator, resurrection, and Adam's future descendants; his unbelief is defiant refusal of God's command and the duty to act, not denial of God or the afterlife.
rows.anchor: İblis esasen Hâlık teâlâ’yı münkir olmadığı gibi ba‘si de münkir değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı infers that Iblis cunningly sought to outlast the first trumpet and escape death forever, though he did not state that aim openly.
rows.anchor: nefha-i ûlâ devresini atlatıp ilelebed ölümden kurtulmayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not categorically reject every plea, even from Iblis whom He expelled, because He knows what is in hearts; He grants him some respite.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir talep ve niyâzını külliyen reddetmek şânından olmayan ve عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ [Âl-i İmrân 3/119]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not grant Iblis's requested endpoint of resurrection, instead setting his reprieve until the known appointed time mentioned in al-Hijr and Sad.
rows.anchor: vakt-i mâlum gününe kadar bir ecel ile inzar buyurdu ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the known time with the first trumpet blast, when those in the heavens and earth are overcome with fear, as described in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: medlûlü üzere nefha-i ûlâ günüdür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as prostration exposed Iblis's nature, his reprieve will become a test for Adam and his descendants.
rows.anchor: İblis’in inzârı da Âdem ve zürriyeti hakkında bir imtihan olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı contrasts Iblis's failure to seek repentance with Adam's haste to ask for forgiveness and mercy, emphasizing the importance of their different responses.
rows.anchor: mukayese edilince aradaki farkın ne kadar mühim olduğu anlaşılır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis frames his vow as a response to God allowing him to go astray and letting him mislead others.
rows.anchor: Öyle ise beni azıtman, iğvâ ve idlâlime[^23] müsaade etmen hakkı için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He vows to ambush humankind on the straight path, which Elmalılı explains as the way of faith, Islam, steadfastness, and access to God's favor.
rows.anchor: Sana, senin nimetine götüren iman ve islâm ve istikāmet yolunu kesip pusuya duracağım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attacking from front, rear, right, and left means striking from every direction an enemy could use to divert and bewilder people.
rows.anchor: dört cihetten yani bir düşmanın hücum edebileceği her taraflarından saldıracağım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says that most people will not be grateful and obedient; Elmalılı reads this as conjecture, since Iblis had seen many sources of evil but only one source of good among humanity.
rows.anchor: âyetinin delâletine göre zannen söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirînin
rows.claim: Some commentators say Iblis learned from the angels that most people would not be grateful.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirînin nakline göre de bunu melâikeden işitip söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God orders Iblis out disgraced and expelled and warns that He will fill Hell with him and every human who follows him; those followers share his fate.
rows.anchor: Demek ki İblis’e uyanlar ondan, onun tebaasından ve onun âkıbetine mahkumdurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God first questioned Iblis instead of expelling him at once; the first order to leave may not yet have been permanent, since repentance and reform could still have led to pardon.
rows.anchor: Birinci فَٱخْرُجْ emrinin ıtlâkına nazaran o lahzada bu ihrâc henüz bir tard-ı müebbed olmamak melhuzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Iblis chose enduring rebellion rather than gratitude and reform, God's later command made his expulsion final and condemned him and his followers to eternal punishment.
rows.anchor: külliyen zemm ü tard ve âhirette de tebaasıyla beraber azâb-ı ebedîye mahkum edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis falls through pride, self-will, and opposition to God's commands; the honor given to Adam brings those traits to light, while Iblis's reprieve creates a balancing trial for human rise or fall.
rows.anchor: İblis’in eceli tehir olunmasında da insanın sukūt veya i‘tilâsına vesile olabilecek bir hikmet-i muvâzene ve ma‘delet vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans and Iblis become trials for one another; people should be grateful for their primordial gift of creation and avoid following Iblis's path lest they share his fall.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı serâzâd kalmak isteyen İblis insan ile mübtelâ olmuş bulunduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who displays one of Iblis's traits has a satanic quality and should work to discipline it.
rows.anchor: şu kıssada İblis’in gösterdiği huylardan hangisi bir kimsede varsa onda şeytandan bir haslet var demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's original station in creation is high and delicate: the angels prostrated while Iblis did not, before Adam and his spouse were told to dwell in the garden.
rows.anchor: İnsanın asl-ı hilkatindeki mevki‘i böyle yüksek ve nâziktir.

rows.speaker: bazı kaviller
rows.claim: One reported view identifies the garden where Adam and his spouse dwelt as the Garden of Eternity.
rows.anchor: cennetü’l-huld[^29] veya semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet

rows.speaker: bazı kaviller
rows.claim: Another reported view identifies Adam's garden as one of the gardens in heaven.
rows.anchor: veya semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet veya Arz cennetlerinden bir cennet

rows.speaker: bazı kaviller
rows.claim: A further reported view identifies Adam's garden as an earthly garden.
rows.anchor: semâ cennetlerinden bir cennet veya Arz cennetlerinden bir cennet olması hakkında bazı kaviller vardır

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the garden from which Iblis was expelled and in which Adam lived was the Garden of Eden, not the Garden of Eternity.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas radıyallâhu anhümâ “cennetü’lhuldde değil cennet-i adnde idiler” demiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With dāl unvowelled, adn means residence and shares a root with maʿdin; the name evokes the garden as the original place of creation and residence, where Adam first received the blessing of existence.
rows.anchor: Dâlin sükûnuyla “Adn” ikāmet demek olduğuna ve “ma‘din” kelimesinin de esası bulunduğuna nazaran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the named gardens of Eden are among the gardens of the afterlife, Elmalılı suggests Adam's first garden was the first garden on the way to the Garden of Eternity, where beginning and return meet, as 43:72 indicates.
rows.anchor: mebde’ ile me‘âdın bir telâkīsi bulunacağı anlaşılabilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the arrogant men addressed by the people of A‘raf as al-Walid b. al-Mughira, Abu Jahl, Amr b. Hisham (As b. Wa’il), and their peers, who boasted that their status mattered more than believers' merit.
rows.anchor: Velîd b. Mugīre, Ebû Cehil, Âs b. Vâil ve akranları

rows.speaker: Velîd b. Mugīre, Ebû Cehil, Âs b. Vâil ve akranları
rows.claim: These leaders scoffed that God might admit Salman, Ammar, and their peers to Paradise while sending them to Hell, insisting God would not prefer their servants and shepherds over them.
rows.anchor: Allah Selman ve Ammar ve emsâllerini cennete koyacak da bizi cehenneme atacak ha, böyle şey olmaz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of A‘raf's rebuke about the uselessness of the arrogant men's group and pride is directed at those leaders and others like them.
rows.anchor: diye bağırdıkları bunlar ve bu gibilerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people pointed to as those whom the leaders thought God would never show mercy are believers such as Salman and Ammar, whom the leaders had scorned.
rows.anchor: onların istihkar ettikleri Selman ve Ammar gibi ehl-i imandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering, the people of Hell politely ask for some water or provision God gave the people of Paradise, and are told that God has forbidden both to disbelievers.
rows.anchor: Lütfen suyunuzdan veya Allah’ın size merzuk kıldığı nimetlerden biraz da bizlere dökün!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the disbelievers as having made play and amusement their religion and having been deceived by worldly life.
rows.anchor: oyunu, eğlenceyi kendilerine din edindiler, ve o dünyâ hayat kendilerini aldattı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His translation preserves the image of God forgetting them on this day, corresponding to their forgetting their meeting with it and denying God's signs.
rows.anchor: biz de bugün onları unutacağız
